title: Manufacturing Science AI — Process Physics & Continuous Improvement Intelligence

units.title: 16 Manufacturing Science AI domains with Claude Opus prompts
units.details: Added 16 MFG-SCIENCE-AI domains: mfg_chip_formation (shear zone mechanics, chip morphology, built-up edge), mfg_cutting_forces (Kienzle/Merchant force models, Fc/Ff/Fp components), mfg_tool_wear (flank/crater wear, Taylor VB progression, tool life prediction), mfg_heat_generation (cutting zone temperatures, heat partition, thermal modeling), mfg_surface_integrity (surface texture, microstructure, hardness alteration), mfg_residual_stress (compressive/tensile stress layers, X-ray diffraction), mfg_burr_formation (exit burr prediction, deburring strategy selection), mfg_material_removal (MRR optimization, specific energy, chip load management), mfg_energy_efficiency (machine energy consumption, idle vs cutting power), mfg_process_capability (Cp/Cpk analysis, process centering, sigma estimation), mfg_statistical_process (SPC charts, control limits, out-of-control detection), mfg_design_of_experiments (full factorial, RSM, Taguchi L-arrays), mfg_lean_manufacturing (7 wastes identification, value-added analysis), mfg_setup_reduction (SMED methodology, internal/external setup), mfg_value_stream (VSM mapping, takt time, flow balance), mfg_continuous_improvement (PDCA, kaizen events, error-proofing/poka-yoke)

references: Machinery's Handbook — chip formation and cutting theory
Boothroyd & Knight — Fundamentals of Machining and Machine Tools

summary: Complete manufacturing science AI intelligence with 16 domains covering chip formation mechanics, cutting force models (Kienzle/Merchant), tool wear progression, heat generation, surface integrity, residual stress, burr formation, material removal optimization, energy efficiency, process capability (Cp/Cpk), statistical process control, design of experiments (DOE/Taguchi), lean manufacturing, SMED setup reduction, value stream mapping, and continuous improvement (PDCA/kaizen). Deep expertise from MIT 2.008 and 2.830J manufacturing courses, Machinery's Handbook, and ISO/ANSI standards.
